title: Bounded loop with fixed iteration cost
statement: Let a program, depth bound, condition $c$, body statement $s$, initial state $\sigma$, time bound $T\in\mathbb N$, postcondition $Q$, invariant predicates $I_i$ on states for natural numbers $i$, and natural numbers $n,b$ be given. If $I_0$ holds at $\sigma$, then for every $i<n$, every state satisfying $I_i$ has a safe condition that holds and admits an execution of $s$ within time $b$ to a state satisfying $I_{i+1}$. If every state satisfying $I_n$ has a safe condition that does not hold and satisfies $Q$, and $n(\operatorname{cost}(c)+1+b)+\operatorname{cost}(c)+1\le T$, then the loop with condition $c$ and body $s$ ends in a state satisfying $Q$ within time $T$.
hypotheses_covered: The invariant $I_0$ holds at the initial state
For every $i<n$ and state satisfying $I_i$, the condition is safe and holds, and the body reaches a state satisfying $I_{i+1}$ within $b$
For every state satisfying $I_n$, the condition is safe and false and $Q$ holds
The stated total loop cost bound is at most $T$
